name_en: Approximation Theorem (Theorem 15.16): the projection is the nearest element of the subspace
name_zh: 逼近定理(定理 15.16):投影是子空间中距离最近的元素
statement: If S is a finite-dimensional subspace of a Euclidean space V and x is in V, then the projection s of x on S satisfies ||x - s|| <= ||x - t|| for every t in S. Equality holds if and only if t = s, so the projection is the unique best approximation to x in S. The proof splits x - t = (x - s) + (s - t) into orthogonal parts and applies the Pythagorean formula.

anchors.quote: THEOREM 15.16. APPROXIMATION THEOREM. Let S be a finite-dimensional subspace of a Euclidean space V, and let x be any element of V.
Then the projection of x on S is nearer to x than any other element of S.
for all $t$ in $S$ ; the equality sign holds if and only if $t = s$ .

name_en: Best approximation of an element by elements of a finite-dimensional subspace
name_zh: 用有限维子空间中的元素对元素作最佳逼近
statement: The approximation problem of the section: given x in a Euclidean space V and a finite-dimensional subspace S, find the element of S that minimizes the norm ||x - t|| over all t in S. 'Nearest' is measured by the norm induced by the inner product; that inner-product structure is not a precondition for stating the problem, which makes sense in any normed linear space, but it is what makes the projection the solution and makes the Pythagorean equality-condition argument available.

anchors.quote: 15.15 Best approximation of elements in a Euclidean space by elements in a finite-dimensional subspace
This is the polynomial of degree $\leq n$ for which the norm $\| f - f_n\|$ is smallest.

statement: An element of the (2n + 1)-dimensional subspace S of C(0, 2pi) spanned by the orthonormal trigonometric functions phi_0, phi_1, ..., phi_{2n} of (15.20); concretely a finite combination (1/2)a_0 + sum_{k=1}^{n} (a_k cos kx + b_k sin kx).

anchors.quote: The $2n + 1$ elements $\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \ldots, \varphi_{2n}$ span a subspace $S$ of dimension $2n + 1$ . The elements of $S$ are called trigonometric polynomials.

statement: The numbers (f, phi_k) obtained by taking the inner product of f with each element of the orthonormal trigonometric set, i.e. (f, phi_k) = integral_0^{2pi} f(x) phi_k(x) dx. They are the coefficients of the projection f_n of f on the span of phi_0, ..., phi_{2n}, and in the cos/sin normalization they become a_k and b_k.

anchors.quote: The numbers $(f, \varphi_k)$ are called Fourier coefficients of $f$ .

name_en: Approximation of continuous functions on [0, 2pi] by trigonometric polynomials
name_zh: 用三角多项式逼近 [0, 2pi] 上的连续函数
statement: Application instance (Example 1) of the Approximation Theorem: in V = C(0, 2pi) with (f, g) = integral_0^{2pi} f g, the projection f_n = sum_{k=0}^{2n} (f, phi_k) phi_k on the span of the orthonormal trigonometric set is the trigonometric polynomial of order n making ||f - f_n|| as small as possible. Rewritten with (15.20) it is the truncated Fourier series (15.22).

anchors.quote: EXAMPLE 1. Approximation of continuous functions on $[0, 2\pi]$ by trigonometric polynomials.
define an inner product by the equation $(f, g) = \int_{0}^{2\pi} f(x)g(x) dx$ .
The approximation theorem tells us that the trigonometric polynomial in (15.22) approximates f better than any other trigonometric polynomial in S

name_en: Approximation of continuous functions on [-1, 1] by polynomials of degree at most n
name_zh: 用次数不超过 n 的多项式逼近 [-1, 1] 上的连续函数
statement: Application instance (Example 2) of the Approximation Theorem: in V = C(-1, 1) with (f, g) = integral_{-1}^{1} f g, the n + 1 normalized Legendre polynomials span the subspace of all polynomials of degree <= n, and the projection f_n = sum_{k=0}^{n} (f, phi_k) phi_k is the polynomial of degree <= n minimizing ||f - f_n||.

anchors.quote: EXAMPLE 2. Approximation of continuous functions on $[-1, 1]$ by polynomials of degree $\leq n$ .
span a subspace S of dimension $n + 1$ consisting of all polynomials of degree $\leq n$ .
This is the polynomial of degree $\leq n$ for which the norm $\| f - f_n\|$ is smallest.

name_en: Nearest linear polynomial to sin(pi t) on [-1, 1]
name_zh: [-1, 1] 上距 sin(pi t) 最近的线性多项式
statement: Worked numerical application instance inside Example 2: for f(x) = sin(pi x) the Legendre coefficients satisfy (f, phi_0) = 0 and (f, phi_1) = sqrt(3/2) * 2/pi, so the nearest linear polynomial is f_1(t) = (3/pi) t; since (f, phi_2) = 0 this is also the nearest quadratic approximation.
